headline: Earnings jump as funding costs ease and buybacks continue
summary_short: First Citizens' Q2 FY2026 net income of $672M rose 25.8% q/q and 16.9% y/y, with diluted EPS of $55.52 up 30.2% q/q as net interest margin held near 3.10% and long-term debt fell 14.9% y/y to roughly $32.0B.
summary_long: Net income of $672M grew 25.8% q/q and 16.9% y/y on higher net interest income (+$35M q/q, aided by lower funding costs after prepaying $2.5B of the Purchase Money Note) and noninterest income (+$84M, driven by a $27M derivative fair-value gain and a $17M tax-credit-investment gain). A $10M benefit for credit losses replaced a $72M linked-quarter provision on a $74M reserve release tied to improved credit quality. Loans grew 1.6% q/q to $151.0B and deposits grew 1.5% q/q to $173.4B. Long-term debt fell 14.9% y/y to roughly $32.0B; the company repurchased $600M of stock and paid a $2.10/share dividend. No forward guidance was issued in this release.
